page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The instance is allocated 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores via hyperthreading, alongside 16 GB of system RAM, yielding a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. The processor configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. The instance includes 3 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and includes no GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent single-core performance alongside typical multi-core scaling limitations inherent to a 4-vCPU allocation. The instance scored 1,556 points in Geekbench single-core testing and achieved an average stress-ng single-core rating of 1,836.48. Multi-threaded metrics reflect the 2-core physical limit, yielding 3,367 points on Geekbench multi-core and a PassMark CPU score of 5,789.76. Memory throughput tests show uncached sequential read speeds of 29.46 GB/sec and write speeds of 23.84 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates steady network and parsing handling, reaching 7.72 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and 3.81 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks.

Without included local NVMe disks, ecs.g7.xlarge relies entirely on network-attached storage, trading raw disk I/O performance for deployment flexibility. From a resource perspective, it offers balanced compute and memory capacity for moderate workloads that do not justify high-density compute or memory-heavy tiers. The instance is suited for general web serving, application middleware, API gateways, light container hosting, and small-scale caching layers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16 GB of memory, and 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no local storage or GPUs, requiring attached network volumes for persistent data. Benchmark metrics reflect balanced performance, displaying solid single-core metrics with an average single-core Geekbench score of 1,556 and 7.72 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, while multi-core workloads are restricted by the 4-thread boundary. The instance provides a cost-effective resource profile for general-purpose application workloads, API backends, web servers, and intermediate caching nodes.
